New description-first implemented responsibility: one allocation, arbitrary finite interleavings, noninterference, correct completed outputs, safe accesses, finite complete schedule and exact trace-derived relational witness. Fixed layout, pointer bounds and scheduling discipline are explicit.

Added pinned-source review of shared-allocation grounding and a documented investigation of byte-source semantics. The byte implementation is deliberately excluded from this first commit; its interpretation issue is recorded rather than resolved by assumption.

The selected tree does not modify existing environment/scoped semantics or descriptors. Scalar shared addresses are checked through explicit extent and 64-bit nonwrapping premises; byte extension changes remain outside this proposal.
No TorchLean tensor interface is implemented by integer vector addition; existing layout/composition promises remain unimplemented.
The shared instruction scheduler is an abstract finite execution discipline, not a CUDA allocator, multi-kernel runtime or hardware launch model.
No automatic backward or authored PTX backward behavior changes.
Only modular integer arithmetic; no floating point, accuracy or PyTorch numerical claims.
Foundation studies remain under PTX semantics; no network application example is implemented.
